items.title: Elephant
items.summary: Elephants are the biggest living land mammals. They have long noses called trunks and large flapping ears.

items.title: Lion
items.summary: The lion (Panthera leo) is a large mammal of the Felidae (cat) family. Some large males weigh over 250 kg (550 lb).

items.title: Tiger
items.summary: The tiger (Panthera tigris) is the largest living member of the cat family, the Felidae. It feeds by hunting, and it lives in Asia.

items.title: Giraffe
items.summary: A giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis) is a mammal which lives in Africa. Giraffes have an even number of toes and are the tallest land animals.

items.title: Blue whale
items.summary: The blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus) is a marine mammal of the suborder of baleen whales (called Mysticeti). They grow to be about 30 m (98 ft) long.

items.title: Gorilla
items.summary: Gorilla is a genus of African apes commonly known as gorillas. They are divided into two species, the western gorilla (Gorilla gorilla) and the eastern gorilla (Gorilla beringei).

items.title: Chimpanzee
items.summary: The common chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), or robust chimpanzee, is a species of great ape. The robust chimpanzee is often just called the chimpanzee (or "chimp"), but this can refer to both species in the genus Pan: the robust chimpanzee and the closely related bonobo.

items.title: Giant panda
items.summary: The giant panda, Ailuropoda melanoleuca, is a bear. It lives in south central China.

items.title: Polar bear
items.summary: The polar bear (Ursus maritimus) is a large bear which lives in the Arctic. It has black skin under the white fur.

items.title: Penguin
items.summary: Penguins are seabirds in the family Spheniscidae. They use their flippers to swim underwater, but they cannot fly in the air.

items.title: Owl
items.summary: Owls are birds in the order Strigiformes. There are 200 species, and they are all animals of prey.

items.title: Shark
items.summary: Sharks are a superorder of fish. This superorder is also known by its scientific name Selachimorpha.

items.title: Dolphin
items.summary: Dolphins are part of the toothed whales. Generally, they are among the smaller whales.

items.title: Octopus
items.summary: Octopus is a genus of cephalopod mollusc in the order Octopoda. The genus is quite typical of most octopods.

items.title: Honey bee
items.summary: A honey bee (or honeybee) is any bee that is a member of the genus Apis. They are all eusocial flying insects which live in colonies of various sizes.

items.title: Butterfly
items.summary: A butterfly is a (usually) day-flying insect of the order Lepidoptera. They are grouped together in the suborder Rhopalocera.

items.title: Crocodile
items.summary: A crocodile is a large amphibious reptile. It lives mostly in large tropical rivers, where it is an ambush predator.

items.title: Komodo dragon
items.summary: The Komodo dragon (Varanus komodoensis) is a species of monitor lizard. They live in the Indonesian islands of Komodo, Rincah, Flores, Gili Motang, and Gili Dasami.

items.title: Cheetah
items.summary: A cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is a medium large cat which lives in Africa and Asia.

items.title: Zebra
items.summary: Zebras are mammals of the family Equidae. Zebras are African horses.

items.title: Kangaroo
items.summary: A kangaroo is an Australian marsupial. It belongs to the genus Macropus.

items.title: Koala
items.summary: Koala (Phascolarctos cinereus) is a plant-eating marsupial. They live in the eucalyptus forests of eastern Australia.

items.title: Platypus
items.summary: The platypus (Ornithorhynchus anatinus), sometimes referred to as the duck-billed platypus, is a small egg laying mammal. It is one of only two monotremes that survive today.

items.title: Wolf
items.summary: The wolf (Canis lupus) is a wild dog of the order Carnivora. It is sometimes called the grey wolf.

items.title: Hippopotamus
items.summary: The hippopotamus (Hippopotamus amphibius), or hippo, ancient Greek for "river horse", also known as the Nile hippopotamus, Common hippopotamus, or River hippopotamus, is a large mammal from Africa that usually eats plants.

items.title: Rhinoceros
items.summary: A rhinoceros (rhino for short) is any animal in the family Rhinocerotidae. They are in the order Perissodactyla, or odd-toed ungulates.

items.title: Camel
items.summary: Camels are mammals of the Camelidae family. Camels form the genus Camelus.

items.title: Bat
items.summary: Bats are mammals in the order Chiroptera. Bats are nocturnal which means they are active during the night, dusk, or dawn and they sleep at day.

items.title: Frog
items.summary: Frogs are amphibians and vertebrates of the order Anura. There is not much difference between frogs and toads, and they are not classified separately.

items.title: Hummingbird
items.summary: Hummingbirds are small birds of the family Trochilidae.
